messages:
Ananya: Quick follow-up from the AuthN/AuthZ RFC — a few unresolved tradeoffs we need to pick for the short migration window. TL;DR: decide key scoping default, service account impersonation surface, and refresh/token lifetimes.
Joel: I skimmed the RFC. My main worry is defaulting to org-scoped API keys — simpler UX but bigger blast radius.
Sam: +1. Org keys are convenient for infra teams, but we already see people accidentally sharing keys in repos. Project-scoped should be the default and org-level keys only with an explicit approval flow.
Michelle: Agreed on project default. Question: how do we handle cross-project services (e.g., billing pipeline reads multiple projects)? Do we give them one org key or a service principal with project grants?
Ananya: Proposal: create service principals (machine users) that can be granted per-project roles. For infra cross-project tasks, we grant the service principal the minimum set of project roles. Org-keys only for org-admins with an RBAC toggle and audit approvals.
Joel: Sounds good. Also, recommend short-lived API keys (1h) with automatic rotation + long-lived refresh tokens for machines. That avoids leaked persistent tokens.
Sam: How do machines authenticate to get a short-lived key? We're leaning toward JWT signed by customer KMS for private deployments, and our internal OAuth for hosted.
Michelle: For hosted, we can implement a token exchange endpoint: POST /v1/token/exchange {grant_type: "service_account_creds"} -> returns short-lived API key. For private, support mTLS client certs or KMS-signed JWTs.
Ananya: We should document the supported flows in the migration guide. Also need compatibility mode: allow current API keys to continue for 90 days with deprecation warnings.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: policy svc-authz-v2 promoted to staging at 2027-05-03T10:30Z
Joel: On RBAC roles: propose these primitives: Viewer (read-only), Invoker (can call APIs), KeyManager (can create/rotate keys), Admin (full). Also a Composite role pattern for common combos.
Sam: One edge: should KeyManager be separate? It might be needed by ops but not by app services. If we keep it separate it's safer.
Michelle: Fine. Also add an "Impersonate" permission so platform teams can request impersonation for day-2 ops; must be scoped and logged.
Ananya: Logging/audit story: every token issuance, rotation, and impersonation must emit an audit entry with requestor, target, reason, and request ID. We'll hook into Console's audit timeline.
Joel: For implementation: phase 1 (2 weeks) - enforce project-default keys + create service-principal API, implement RBAC role skeleton. Phase 2 (4 weeks) - short-lived keys + token-exchange endpoint + audit logs. Phase 3 - org-key approval workflow and private deployment JWT/mTLS options.
Sam: Action items: @Joel to draft endpoint spec for token exchange, @Michelle to draft migration docs + deprecation plan, @Ananya to produce RBAC policy schemas and audit event model.
Michelle: I'll also set up a customer-visible FAQ about why we moved away from org-defaults and how to migrate.
Ananya: Great. Let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to approve the phase 1 design and owners. Meeting invite incoming. :thumbsup:
Joel: Thanks — will post the token-exchange API draft in #devex after the meeting.
